answer: Each node carries a signed lantern token issued by a consensus vertex that records the cumulative work and reputation of the identity. When an agent proposes a transaction, the protocol aggregates the tokens of all identities behind it and applies a quadratic weighting function, so ten freshly‑minted tokens from a Sybil orchard contribute only the square‑root of their count, while a single long‑standing token retains full weight. An attacker must therefore invest the square of the desired influence, making large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
